body.statement: If Open-ended Question 1 has an affirmative answer, the resulting finite selector satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-\theta(P)|\le C_{\mathrm{upper}}\rho_\star,\qquad R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.\] This strictly extends the nonprivate frontier of Kennedy et al. on the exact-uniform two-scale subclass by identifying and attaining both pure-privacy branches, and it holds without a nuisance-sieve logarithm.
body.justification: The theorem is the matched sparse-to-dense minimax statement and makes the privacy elbows the paper's named focal object.
body.gap: Kennedy et al. establish the nonprivate pointwise rate, and Schröder et al. establish approximate-private releases; neither gives a pure-private minimax law over the full unknown-propensity Hölder class.
body.consumer: Researchers releasing individualized treatment effects obtain a principled resolution and privacy calibration rather than a learner-specific noise heuristic.
